title: Mobile-sign by-law change comes from SPC; a councillor says his amendment was made there, not in public
summary: By-law 2066 (one-year permits for mobile signs) came to council 'as per recommendation from council SPC meeting' of December 8, 2015. Councillor Jac Siemens opposed the 365-day term but said he would not repeat at the public meeting the amendment he had already pushed at the Strategic Priorities Committee (SPC). First reading carried with at least two councillors opposed.
status_detail: First reading carried December 15, 2015, with a public hearing to follow. The SPC debate and the fate of Siemens's amendment there are not in the public record; only the result reached council.
figures: Permit term 365 days (transcript 2015-12-15, 0:16:40).
reasons: efficiency: Did not re-move at the public meeting an amendment already argued at SPC. (Jac Siemens)
public: No members of the public spoke on this item.
vote: carried; at least 2 against (Jac Siemens and one unidentified councillor)
notes: The December 8, 2015 SPC meeting date comes from the City Manager's introduction; no SPC minutes were found.

title: Budgets built over months of study sessions; the public hearing is the first public look
summary: Each year's financial plan was worked on from July to November in study sessions and presented at a single public hearing for approval. The Mayor said the room was normally empty; in 2017 a councillor said council had 'seen all these numbers before'; in 2018 the Director of Finance said the plan was based on council's 'final review in November'.
status_detail: Budgets were presented and voted on publicly (with an open house in 2016), but the line-by-line choices were made earlier in closed sessions.
figures: 2018 capital program $17.2M; revenues just under $29M (Director of Finance, 2018-03-20 0:00:58).
reasons: efficiency: The budget is the culmination of many decisions made over many meetings. (Chris Goertzen)
public: Few residents attended; one delegate asked about a grant request in 2018.

title: Councillor says changes to city standards are discussed at SPC, not at council meetings
summary: Council approved a one-time exception to the city's servicing standards for a commercial development (through a development agreement), against administration's warning that it would set a precedent. Councillor Jac Siemens said a change to the standard itself would be discussed at SPC, 'where we get full response from staff', not at a council meeting.
status_detail: Exception approved by voice vote at the public meeting; no public follow-up on the standard itself was found in this period.
reasons: staff-direction: Policy changes to city standards belong at SPC, where council gets full staff input. (Jac Siemens)
public: The developer spoke for the request; no objectors are recorded in the passage read.
vote: carried ('Opposed? That's carried'; count not recorded)
notes: Meeting chaired by the Deputy Mayor (John Fehr was Deputy Mayor 2015-2017).

title: Mayor gives short public summaries of the all-day summer study sessions
summary: After the all-day closed summer study sessions (July 5, 2016 at Mennonite Heritage Village; July 4, 2017), Mayor Chris Goertzen opened or closed the evening meeting with a short account: vision and 'big picture' (2016); the 2018 capital plan and budget highlights and a dated timeline of the performing arts centre (2017). No agenda, minutes or materials from the sessions were found in the public record.
status_detail: Highlights were reported orally; what was discussed and any direction given to staff are not public.
figures: One summer study session per year; Siemens counted 16 study sessions over 2010-2018 (see 2018-meeting-count).

title: Items settled at SPC adopted in public with a one-line explanation
summary: Several items came to council already agreed at SPC and passed with brief explanations and no recorded dissent: Main Street East parking restrictions (2016, with 2014 SPC minutes in the package), the 'More for you here' slogan (2017), parking-fine changes (2017) and road renaming in the annexed area (2018).
status_detail: All carried; in one case (2016) old SPC minutes were placed in the public package.
notes: Slogan item (2017-06-20, 0:50:35) was introduced by an unidentified mover as 'discussed at a Strategic Priority Committee meeting'.

title: A councillor wanted mobile-sign rules hashed out at SPC; the Mayor kept the debate in the public meeting
summary: When amendments to the mobile-sign rules (By-law 2065) came up, a councillor said they would have preferred 'a more informal setting, in an SPC or a special meeting'. Mayor Chris Goertzen replied that council could hear and discuss it at the meeting, which 'is public, it is recorded', and council worked through the options section by section in public.
status_detail: Options were debated in the open meeting and council gave direction by consensus and vote.
reasons: candid-discussion: Preferred an SPC or special meeting for 'a bit more casual discussion'. (unidentified councillor)
public: Administration said the options reflected submissions from businesses and the Steinbach Chamber of Commerce.
notes: The councillor at 0:24:01 could not be identified; quote not for named use.

title: Development-fee by-laws renewed as recommended by the Strategic Priorities Committee
summary: By-laws 2070 and 2071 renewed the residential and non-residential capital development fees to the end of 2019 with 2.5% yearly increases. The Mayor said council had discussed it 'a week back at Strategic Priority Committee' and administration said the committee's recommendations were written into the by-law. Both passed with short public reasons and no dissent heard.
status_detail: Both by-laws carried at the public meeting; the SPC discussion that shaped them is not public.
figures: 2.5% increase per year; fee schedule renewed for 3 years to end of 2019 (transcript 2016-10-04, 0:09:24 and 0:11:07).
public: No members of the public spoke.
notes: SPC date approximated as one week before (about Sept 27, 2016) from the Mayor's words.

title: Organizational meetings: procedure by-laws kept unchanged; city manager files a voluntary public declaration
summary: The Municipal Act requires each council to review its organizational by-law (2025) and procedure by-law (1809) once a term. On November 7, 2017, with both Councillors Penner absent, both were presented 'for council's information' and kept without discussion or change. A month later, By-law 2025's rule on keeping closed-meeting matters confidential was at the centre of the golf-course dispute. At the 2016 organizational meeting the City Manager filed a voluntary declaration of his community involvements 'for public disclosure'.
status_detail: No changes were proposed; no motion was needed.

title: $24.3-million arts centre estimate reached the public outside a council meeting; council reaffirmed its share 4-3
summary: A Class C estimate of $24.3 million for the performing arts centre (earlier planning assumed about $15 million) was presented to council in November 2016 and to stakeholders, then reached the media before any public council meeting. On December 20, 2016 the Mayor rebuked members for going to the media first; Councillors Zwaagstra and Susan Penner said the figure had never been debated or voted on at an open meeting. Council reaffirmed its $7.5 million share with a June 30, 2017 deadline, 4-3.
status_detail: The estimate was first debated at a public meeting on December 20, 2016, after it had gone to council in a non-public setting (November 2016, per the Mayor's July 4, 2017 timeline). Funding was not in place by June 30, 2017 and the project lapsed, which the Mayor announced publicly on July 4, 2017.
figures: Class C estimate $24.3M vs. earlier outer limit of about $15M (Zwaagstra, transcript 2016-12-20 0:44:53); city share capped at $7.5M with sunset June 30, 2017 (0:41:13). SteinbachOnline (Dec 20, 2016): $17.9M building + $6.4M site, equipment and engineering.
reasons: candid-discussion: Members should raise disagreements with council before speaking to the media, and respect decisions already voted. (Chris Goertzen); no-decision-made: Council only ever committed $7.5M, so the higher estimate changed nothing council had decided. (John Fehr)
public: No residents spoke. Who first gave the estimate to the media is not stated in the transcript. SteinbachOnline (Dec 20, 2016) reported Susan Penner publicly calling for the plan to be dropped.
vote: 4-3 (against: Susan Penner, Michael Zwaagstra, Earl Funk)
decision_source: transcript; split and names confirmed by SteinbachOnline, Dec 20, 2016
notes: Transcripts of the public meetings from Oct 4 to Dec 6, 2016 contain no mention of the performing arts centre. The 2017 financial plan (Feb 21, 2017) carried with Zwaagstra and Funk speaking against because of the $24M PAC; the full vote count is not in the transcript.

title: Golf club land bought for $500,000 and leased back for $1 a year after a year of closed meetings
themes: in-camera; land; grants; documents; objection; reasons-given
summary: The Steinbach Fly-In Golf Club first asked council, in a closed meeting about a year earlier, for a $500,000 grant, which was refused. After further closed meetings it became a $500,000 purchase of 40 acres of the course, leased back for about 63 years. Supplementary information reached council the day before and the lease was not in the printed package. The deal was first made public on December 5, 2017 and approved 4-3 the same night; Zwaagstra, Funk and Susan Penner objected to the closed process.
status_detail: Purchase and leaseback approved December 5, 2017; possession March 1, 2018. The first payment (about $167,000) was in the 2018 financial plan (see 2018-golf-payment-in-budget).
figures: $500,000 for 40 acres; lease about 63 years to about 2083 (City Manager, transcript 0:58:52); lease $1 a year (Zwaagstra 1:07:14); payments changed from 5 to 3 years, about $100,000 to nearly $170,000 a year (Zwaagstra 1:07:55); land-purchase budget $300,000 a year (Fehr 1:01:04). Value: Fehr 'upwards of $1 million'; Funk and Zwaagstra said no appraisal was done; Cari Penner said 'the actual appraisal of the land' was much higher than the offer.
reasons: confidential-land: Every land deal is negotiated behind closed doors; discussing it first is 'not prudent' because of competition. (John Fehr); confidential-land: It was 'negotiated like every other land deal'. (Chris Goertzen)
public: No public input before the vote; objectors said it was the first time the public heard of the deal. Zwaagstra's claim that payments were moved to 3 years to avoid Municipal Board scrutiny was disputed by an interjection in the room ('That's not avoid true'); unproven. The appraisal question is unresolved in the record.
vote: 4-3 (against: Michael Zwaagstra, Earl Funk, Susan Penner); lease carried separately, Zwaagstra against, full count not recorded
notes: Golf club's grant request: 'just over a year' before Dec 5, 2017 (Zwaagstra), so first_date is approximate. No minutes exist for Dec 5, 2017; decision from the transcript.

title: Council pay: task-force report in public, discussion at SPC, by-law debated and passed in public
summary: A citizen task force on council pay presented its report at the April 18, 2017 public meeting; the Mayor said it would go on 'an SPC agenda'. The resulting By-law 2084 (pay tied to a share of MLA salaries) was debated and amended in public on June 6 and passed third reading June 20. The roughly $20,000 not in the 2017 budget was sent to the study session to find savings.
status_detail: By-law 2084 passed June 20, 2017, effective July 2017; where the $20,000 came from was left to the study session.
figures: About $20,000 unbudgeted for the rest of 2017 (City Manager, transcript 2017-06-20 0:57:22).
public: Task-force members presented publicly (citizens; not named here).

title: Public requests and letters routinely referred to study sessions
summary: Council regularly sent items raised at public meetings to the next study session: a funding application (June 2017), a resident's request for a Clearspring sidewalk (June 5, 2018, by vote), a provincial infrastructure call for proposals (June 19, 2018) and the arts centre grant (June 19, 2018). Outcomes came back only when the item later returned to a public agenda.
status_detail: No public report-back on these study-session discussions was found in the meetings searched, except the arts centre grant.
reasons: candid-discussion: Long-standing items need fuller discussion at study session. (Jac Siemens)
public: A resident's letter (correspondence item 11D, June 5, 2018) asked for a sidewalk to Clearspring.
notes: 'this school's' in the Siemens quote is the transcript's wording (likely 'this goes').

title: Grant requests 'taken as information' in public and decided at the November budget study session
summary: Grant letters from groups (Chamber of Commerce, Youth for Christ, Envision, Mennonite Heritage Village and others) were routinely 'taken as information' at public meetings and dealt with in the November study session and the budget. Susan Penner described the cycle in 2018; Earl Funk contrasted the seniors' centre's public request with the golf club's closed-door one.
status_detail: Results appear in the adopted budget; the deliberation and reasons for each request are not public.
reasons: efficiency: Requests are weighed together when the budget is prepared. (Chris Goertzen)
public: A delegate for the Pat Porter Active Living Centre asked at the 2018 budget hearing when council would answer its request.

title: Funk asks when matters from closed meetings may be debated in public
summary: Two weeks before the golf-course land deal came to a public meeting, Councillor Earl Funk quoted By-law 2025 (the duty to keep closed-meeting matters confidential) and asked when a matter discussed with an outside group becomes public. City Manager Troy Warkentin said closed matters stay closed until council as a body decides to bring them into an open meeting.
status_detail: Question answered on the spot; no change to the rules followed.
reasons: municipal-act-allows: Under the Municipal Act and By-law 2025, closed matters stay confidential until council as a body brings them into an open meeting. (Troy Warkentin)
notes: Meeting chaired by the Deputy Mayor (Cari Penner, appointed Nov 7, 2017).

title: Motion to have the golf club present its request at a public meeting was defeated 4-3 behind closed doors
summary: At one of the closed meetings on the Steinbach Fly-In Golf Club proposal, Councillor Michael Zwaagstra moved that the club's board be asked to present at a public council meeting, with a couple of weeks for public feedback before a decision. By the account of Zwaagstra and Councillor Earl Funk on December 5, 2017, it was defeated 4-3. The closed-meeting vote is not in any public record found.
status_detail: Defeated in a closed meeting (date unknown, 2017); the deal first appeared in public on the night of the vote.
reasons: confidential-land: Land deals are never discussed until made; 'not prudent' because of competing interest (said in reply on Dec 5, 2017). (John Fehr); municipal-act-allows: Said the Municipal Act kept him from speaking publicly until the item reached a public meeting. (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: No public input was taken.
vote: defeated 4-3 (individual votes not public; Zwaagstra and Funk in favour by their own account)
notes: The date of the closed meeting and the names of the four members who voted against are not public.

title: Zwaagstra reads municipal-governance advice against closed meetings to open a council meeting
summary: Two months after the golf deal, Councillor Michael Zwaagstra opened the February 6, 2018 meeting by reading George Cuff's guide for municipal leaders: council decisions on public issues are to be made publicly with very few exceptions, and closed meetings on controversial issues provoke the public. He added that it is good the meetings are recorded for YouTube and that hiding information breeds mistrust.
status_detail: A statement only; no change to procedure followed in this term.
notes: The first quote is Zwaagstra reading from Cuff, not his own wording.

title: 2018 budget passes 4-3; three members vote no over the golf payment and the closed process behind it
summary: The 2018 financial plan raised the mill rate by 0.16 and carried the first golf-land payment. Councillors Funk, Zwaagstra and Susan Penner voted against, citing the closed meetings and the 4-3 refusal of a public presentation. Councillor John Fehr replied that land deals are always done in camera and the issue was settled. Administration said removing the payment was not an option because the agreement was signed.
status_detail: Financial plan approved (R18-056, 4-3). The tax levy by-law then passed first and third reading 5-2 (R18-081, R18-096) and second reading 4-3 (R18-082).
figures: Mill rate 14.09, up 0.16 (Director of Finance, 0:00:58); first golf payment about $160,000-$170,000 (0:15:07); 0.1 mill is about $150,000 (0:14:47); Zwaagstra: $167,000 this year.
reasons: confidential-land: 'You cannot make a land deal in the public eye.' (John Fehr); already-public-later: The deal was voted on; opponents should move on. (John Fehr)
public: A delegate for the Pat Porter Active Living Centre asked whether its grant-in-lieu request was in the budget; the Mayor said grant policy had not changed. Susan Penner said residents had told her they opposed the golf payment.
vote: 4-3 (against: Michael Zwaagstra, Susan Penner, Earl Funk)
notes: Diarization mixes labels in this file (H is used for both Fehr and Zwaagstra); speakers assigned from who was called on.

title: New zoning by-law and community plan: reviewed at SPC, then open houses and public hearings
summary: After annexation, the zoning by-law (2100), official community plan (2099) and building by-law were reviewed at committee (including the SPC of March 27, 2018), then taken to open houses and public hearings. The one issue not settled at committee, hard-surfacing of parking, was debated and voted on in public (4-2).
status_detail: First reading June 5, 2018; public hearing July 17, 2018. Surfacing option chosen by recorded vote R18-128.
reasons: already-public-later: Committee work was followed by an open house, public debate and a public hearing. (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: Residents spoke at the July 17, 2018 hearing (not named here).

title: Arts centre matching grant tabled to the study session 4-3, then approved in public after a delegation
summary: Councillor Susan Penner moved, without notice, to match the Steinbach Arts Council's $65,000 Co-op Community Spaces grant from the recreation and culture reserve. Councillors Fehr and Zwaagstra wanted more detail and a proper policy change; the Mayor suggested tabling to the July study session, and the motion was tabled 4-3. On September 4 the Arts Council presented its plans as a public delegation and the grant passed unanimously.
status_detail: Tabled June 19 (R18-148, 4-3); approved unanimously September 4, 2018 (R18-205) after the Arts Council answered council's questions in public. Whether it was discussed at the July study session is not in the public record.
figures: $65,000 matched from the Recreation and Culture reserve (minutes R18-205); grant to be spent within 2 years (City Manager, 2018-06-19 1:03:43).
reasons: staff-direction: A change in grant policy should be done properly, with details on lease responsibilities, before deciding. (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: The Steinbach Arts Council presented as a delegation on September 4, 2018.
vote: table 4-3 (against: Susan Penner, Cari Penner, Earl Funk); approval unanimous

title: Downtown land purchases brought to public meetings with prices and recorded votes
summary: Administration negotiated conditional offers on homes near the T.G. Smith Centre under a 25-year downtown land strategy and brought each to a public meeting with the price: 336 Hanover ($194,500), 332 Hanover ($172,900) and 380 Hanover ($280,000). Each passed with a recorded vote; John Fehr voted against all three, saying the city was over its land budget and pushing residents out of downtown.
status_detail: R18-152 (5-1), R18-174 (5-1), R18-238 (6-1); reasons for and against given in public.
mover: Earl Funk; Cari Penner; Cari Penner
seconder: Michael Zwaagstra; Susan Penner; Susan Penner
notes: Contrast with the golf purchase: these came with prices and reasons at an ordinary public meeting.

title: Siemens tallies 190 council meetings, 80 SPC meetings and 16 study sessions over two terms
summary: At the last meeting of the 2010-2018 council, Councillor Jac Siemens counted 190 council meetings, 80 SPC meetings and 16 study sessions over 8 years, and said Mayor Goertzen had chaired over 288 council meetings and 120 SPC meetings since 2000. He also noted that 'each word is recorded'.
status_detail: Figures from a farewell speech; not checked against city records.
figures: 190 council meetings, 80 SPC meetings, 16 study sessions (2010-2018); Mayor: 288+ council meetings, 120 SPC meetings (transcript 2018-10-16 0:00:23 and 0:55:08).

title: Budgets and spending priorities are built at closed study sessions every year
summary: Throughout the term, council built each year's budget and capital list at multi-day study sessions (the first in November 2018, a summer session each July, a fall session each November) that are not recorded, minuted or open to the public. Members referred to them openly in public meetings; the financial plan itself was then presented at a public hearing and adopted by resolution each spring.
status_detail: Every financial plan in the term was adopted unanimously in public (2019 R19-063, 2020 R20-074, 2021 and 2022 by unnumbered resolutions in the parsed minutes), but the trade-offs were settled at the study sessions; no study-session agenda, minutes or recording was found.
figures: 2020 capital program $13.1M; 2021 $19.6M (financial plan presentations, transcripts 2020-04-07, 2021-04-06).
reasons: efficiency: budget-making is a year-long process starting in May; study sessions are where the work is done (Jac Siemens); already-public-later: the finished budget comes to a public hearing and vote (Mayor Earl Funk)
public: No resident comment on the study-session process was found in this period.
notes: Study-session dates come from members' remarks; none were found on any public calendar or agenda for 2018–2022.

title: Council pay raise to offset the federal tax change, funded "within our current budget" as agreed beforehand
summary: By-law 2110 raised council pay so that take-home pay stayed the same after Ottawa ended the tax-free one-third allowance. Councillor Siemens explained the change in public, citing the pledge to be "open and transparent", and said it had already been agreed that the cost would be absorbed within the budget.
status_detail: First and second readings Dec 4, 2018 (R18-280, R18-281); third reading Dec 18, 2018 (R18-294), all unanimous.
figures: About $200/month per councillor, $400 for the mayor; budget impact about $28,000 a year (Siemens, transcript 0:45:03).
reasons: already-public-later: explained the reasons in public because members had promised openness (Jac Siemens)
public: No public comment recorded.
seconder: Michael Zwaagstra / Damian Penner / Jac Siemens
notes: Where "it was agreed" is not stated; the timing points to the November 2018 budget study session.

title: A resident's garbage-service complaint at a public hearing is pointed to "a council committee meeting", then to staff
summary: At the Dec 4, 2018 hearing on garbage rates, a resident raised a separate service problem. The mayor first said it would "most likely" go to an SPC-type "council committee meeting"; the City Manager suggested staff follow up instead, and the mayor agreed.
status_detail: Referred to administration for follow-up by letter; no public report back was found.
reasons: staff-direction: issue unrelated to the by-law; left with administration (Mayor Earl Funk)
public: A resident (initials not recorded clearly in the transcript) raised a pickup problem; two other residents objected to flat garbage fees.
notes: Transcript renders SPC as "SBA"/"CPC".

title: Motion to send the purchasing by-law to a closed SPC meeting defeated 3–4; by-law passed in public
summary: Before second reading of Purchasing and Tendering By-law 2108 (raising the City Manager's spending authority from $250,000 to $350,000), Councillor Jake Hiebert moved to postpone it to an SPC meeting so new councillors could ask questions. Councillor Zwaagstra argued the change was simple, packages come in advance and questions can be asked any time; the mayor agreed. The referral failed and the by-law passed unanimously.
status_detail: R19-011 (postpone to SPC) defeated 3–4; second and third readings (R19-012, R19-013) and the policy (R19-014) carried unanimously the same night.
figures: City Manager purchasing authority $250,000 → $350,000; managers $10,000 → $15,000; designated staff $50,000 → $75,000 (Warkentin, transcript 0:54:46).
reasons: candid-discussion: new councillors needed a fuller discussion at SPC before deciding (Jake Hiebert); efficiency: against the referral: not complex, packages arrive in advance, questions can go to the City Manager (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: None.
vote: 3-4 defeated (for: J. Hiebert, J. Siemens, B. Hiebert; against: S. Penner, M. Zwaagstra, E. Funk, D. Penner)

title: Pool fee increase: "significant discussion and debate" at SPC, no questions in public, unanimous
summary: The first pool fee increase in about ten years was debated at a Strategic Priorities Committee meeting and sent to council "at the recommendation of committee". The SPC report itself was copied into the public package. At the public meeting there were no questions; two councillors and the mayor spoke in favour and it passed unanimously.
status_detail: R19-022 carried unanimously; new fees effective April 1, 2019.
figures: Increases from $0 (youth) to $4.76 before tax (new child fee); expected revenue about $80,000 (mayor); pool deficit over $800,000 a year (D. Penner).
reasons: already-public-later: the SPC report was included in the public package (Troy Warkentin, City Manager)
public: None.

title: RCMP commander asks to go "in camera" during a delegation; the mayor points out the meeting is on video
summary: During the RCMP annual presentation, the detachment commander asked whether he could speak "in camera" and asked the media not to report some remarks. The mayor and a councillor replied that the meeting was on video; he continued in general terms instead. Council did not close the meeting.
status_detail: The meeting stayed open; the remarks were made in general terms on the record.
public: H.L. (RCMP detachment commander, delegation) asked to speak off the record.
notes: The delegate is identified by initials under the report's rule for delegations.

title: Business tax and economic development recommendations held for the July study session ("can't say right now publicly")
summary: Presenting the "Why Steinbach" economic development website, Councillor Susan Penner said council would decide at the July study session whether to keep the business tax, and that further infrastructure recommendations would be brought there that she could not yet describe publicly.
status_detail: The business tax continued at 0.5% (2020 levy By-law 2151, first reading May 5, 2020; 2021 By-law 2172). The other study-session recommendations were not identified in public.
figures: Business tax 0.5% (Warkentin, 2020-05-05 transcript 0:27:23).
reasons: no-decision-made: recommendations not yet put to council, so not described publicly (Susan Penner)
public: None.

title: Councillor Susan Penner explains in-camera meetings: labour, legal and land, with "transparency after the fact"
themes: in-camera; reasons-given; good-practice; land; personnel; legal
summary: In her opening remarks, Councillor Susan Penner explained why council meets in camera (labour, legal and land), said giving reasons for decisions matters, and acknowledged that in such cases "the transparency has to come after the fact". She described decisions as made "at public meetings or in camera".
status_detail: A public explanation; no change to practice. No in-camera resolution appears in any 2018–2022 minutes.
reasons: confidential-land: land prices would be inflated if purchases were known (Susan Penner); confidential-personnel: union contract negotiations (Susan Penner); legal-advice: lawsuits (Susan Penner); already-public-later: residents can understand decisions once information is made public (Susan Penner)
public: None.

title: Major items decided on packages council received the same day (2019–2022)
summary: Several significant decisions were made on material that reached council (and was not in the public agenda package) the day of the meeting: the event centre MOU (Oct 1, 2019), the Clearspring options report (Jan 21, 2020), the $1.28M aquatic centre renovation tender (June 2, 2020), the Code of Conduct final readings (Oct 20, 2020), the $1.9M event centre design contract (Sept 21, 2021) and a $1.4M land purchase (Apr 19, 2022). All passed unanimously.
status_detail: All approved unanimously at the same meeting (R19-193, R20-012, R20-118, R20-208, R21-199, R22-103).
figures: Aquatic tender $1,283,415, project budget $1,479,415 (R20-118); design contract $1,898,430 (R21-199); land $1.4M (R22-103).
reasons: efficiency: tender and negotiation timing; packages provided as soon as available (Troy Warkentin, City Manager)
public: None.
seconder: Susan Penner / Jac Siemens / Susan Penner
notes: See also 2019-event-centre-mou, 2020-clearspring-greens-levy and 2020-code-of-conduct-ethics-commission for the other same-day items.

title: Event centre agreement: $10 million commitment approved the night its package arrived, after months of private talks
summary: The Southeast Event Centre memorandum of understanding came to council as "information to follow"; the City Manager said the package reached council "earlier this evening, just prior to council meeting". The group had approached council months earlier. After a presentation and speeches from every member, council approved the MOU and the grant application unanimously; the mayor said he did not need to convince council. At the 2021 borrowing hearing he said council had "unanimously chose to go in this direction" as the project was discussed.
status_detail: R19-193 (MOU) and R19-198 (ICIP grant application) carried unanimously Oct 1, 2019; borrowing By-law 2186 had no objectors at its Dec 7, 2021 hearing and passed third reading Apr 19, 2022 (R22-100).
figures: Total $42.5M: city $10M plus $500,000/year, $17.5M federal/provincial grant sought, $15M private donations (mayor and SEC presentation, transcript 0:51:37); borrowing $7.5M (2021-12-07, 0:06:16).
reasons: already-public-later: the decision and its terms were announced and explained at the public meeting (Mayor Earl Funk)
public: G.L. and K.G. presented for Southeast Event Centre Inc. (organization may be named). No resident objected at the 2021 borrowing hearing.
notes: Which Councillor Penner named the four strategic priorities could not be confirmed (low confidence; not for publication).

title: Clearspring Greens pathway levy: cost split "deliberated" privately, lot bought "privately and quietly", reversed after meeting residents
summary: A $625,000 local-improvement pathway would have charged 146 Clearspring Greens lots about $4,280 each. At the Jan 7, 2020 hearing the mayor said council had "deliberated on numbers" for two years and settled on roughly an 80/20 split, and that the land purchase had to be done "privately and quietly". Siemens' amendment to cut costs failed 2–5 and second reading passed 5–2. Two weeks later, on a staff report emailed the same day, council moved the $208,000 lighting cost to the city (6–1), the mayor saying council changed its mind after meeting "with the community".
status_detail: The cost to residents was cut, but 78 objections followed and council cancelled the plan on Jan 5, 2021 (R21-011) in favour of a 50/50 plan (see 2021-clearspring-revised-plan).
figures: Estimated cost $625,000; $4,280.82 upfront or $1,044.05/yr per lot (Warkentin, 2020-01-07, 0:09:47); lighting $208,000 moved to city, per-home cost about $2,800 (Zwaagstra, 2020-01-21, 0:07:01); 32 objections then (0:14:30); lot at 42 Carleton Dr bought for $115,972.50 (R19-194, 2019-10-01).
reasons: confidential-land: the lot purchase could not be announced or the price would rise (Mayor Earl Funk); confidential-land: no public announcement of a land purchase (Michael Zwaagstra); efficiency: an open community session would not produce consensus on route or lighting (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: Residents (delegation July 16, 2019 led by M.F.) asked for a safe pathway; at the Jan 7, 2020 hearing many objected to the cost and asked why the developer had not paid; some called it unfair compared with other neighbourhoods (residents' claims).
vote: R20-005 5-2 (against: Siemens, J. Hiebert); amendment defeated 2-5 (for: Siemens, J. Hiebert); R20-012 6-1 (against: Siemens)
notes: Zwaagstra said "as we said last week" on Jan 21, 2020, and Damian Penner referred to an SPC "last week"; whether the lighting change was discussed at that SPC could not be confirmed.

title: SPC "collectively chose" to keep routine excavator licences on the public agenda
summary: Damian Penner said that at the previous week's SPC, staff asked whether excavator licences should stay on the council agenda, and council "collectively chose" to keep them there.
status_detail: Licences stayed on the public agenda and were approved.
reasons: staff-direction: staff sought council direction at SPC on agenda practice (Damian Penner)
public: None.
notes: Light-hearted exchange; included because it records an SPC direction.

title: Deputy Mayor Zwaagstra warns against "decisions behind closed doors" and says SPC meetings are open to the public
themes: spc; recording; objection; good-practice; reasons-given; personnel; land; legal
summary: In his opening, Councillor Zwaagstra said all local politicians must resist the temptation to decide behind closed doors, that only personnel, land and legal matters belong there, and that "our regular council meetings and SPC meetings" are open to the media and the public and recorded. The mayor thanked him for the reminder "to keep public business done in public".
status_detail: Council meetings were recorded and posted. No public notice, agenda, minutes or recording of an SPC meeting was found for 2018–2022, so the statement that SPC is open to the public could not be confirmed.
reasons: confidential-personnel: specific personnel issues (Michael Zwaagstra); confidential-land: possible land purchases or sales (Michael Zwaagstra); legal-advice: legal matters (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: None.
notes: Zwaagstra quoted a municipal governance expert ("controversial ... doesn't make it confidential"); name as transcribed is uncertain.

title: Traffic problems discussed at study and long-term planning sessions rather than in public
summary: Responding to residents' traffic concerns at hearings, the mayor and Councillor Siemens said council discusses traffic at study sessions and long-term planning sessions, including one planned for November 2022.
status_detail: No public traffic plan resulting from those sessions was found in this period.
reasons: no-decision-made: ongoing long-term planning (Jac Siemens)
public: Residents at the Sept 6, 2022 Loewen Boulevard hearing raised traffic and access concerns (residents' claims).

title: COVID-19: mayor given power to postpone meetings; meetings kept going and livestreamed
summary: On March 17, 2020 council let the mayor change, postpone or cancel the April meetings with 72 hours' notice, and recessed every few minutes for distancing. From April 7, 2020 meetings were livestreamed. No regular meeting in spring 2020 was found to have been cancelled. In 2022 councillors asked when chambers could return to normal.
status_detail: R20-065 carried unanimously; April 7 and 21, 2020 meetings were held (transcripts and minutes exist).
reasons: efficiency: otherwise a special meeting would be needed just to cancel a meeting (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: Applicants and objectors continued to appear in person, masked at the podium in 2021.
notes: Whether the public gallery was closed during 2020–2021 could not be confirmed from the transcripts or minutes.

title: Closed ("in-camera") meetings held after adjournment, with no closure resolution in the minutes
summary: On May 5, 2020 the mayor adjourned and announced council would "reconvene here for a in-camera meeting"; on Oct 5, 2021 he announced "a short closed meeting". Neither set of minutes records a resolution to close, the ground under s. 152(3), or the general nature of the matter; no 2018–2022 minutes do.
status_detail: No minuted closure or report of any outcome was found.
public: None.
notes: Subjects unknown; closures may have been for lawful reasons (personnel, legal, land), but the minutes do not say.

title: Design and construction standards: "consensus among council" at SPC, summary only in the public package
summary: Revisions to the city's engineering standards for new development were presented in detail at the May 12, 2020 SPC, where staff said council reached consensus. The public package carried only a summary; council adopted them unanimously with one brief comment.
status_detail: R20-119 carried unanimously. The same pattern recurred in Feb 2024 (existing report, Case 3).
reasons: already-public-later: a summary of the changes was in the public package (Troy Warkentin, City Manager)
public: None.

title: Dwelling Unit Safety Standards by-law drafted on SPC direction; the SPC report was in the public package
summary: The safety standards by-law for secondary suites was first presented at the May 12, 2020 SPC, where council directed staff to draft it. At first reading Councillor Siemens explained it in public and pointed residents to the SPC report in the package.
status_detail: First reading R20-167 (Sept 1, 2020); second and third readings R21-007, R21-008 (Jan 5, 2021), all unanimous.
reasons: staff-direction: council direction given at committee to prepare the by-law (Troy Warkentin, City Manager)
public: None.

title: Community funding requests routinely sent to study sessions and decided there
summary: Requests from STARS (Sept 2020), Steinbach and Area Animal Rescue ($20,000, Mar 2021), the Pat Porter Active Living Centre (Oct 2021) and STARS again (Sept 2022) were sent to a study session rather than decided in public. The Handy Transit grant to Serving Seniors was agreed at a study session and the resulting agreement approved in public. Grants appear publicly only in an annual after-the-fact summary.
status_detail: STARS received $15,829 in 2021 (grants summary R22-066, Mar 15, 2022), the $1-per-capita decision having been made at the fall 2020 study session (STARS delegate, 2022-09-20). Handy Transit agreement approved R21-253. No public decision on the Animal Rescue or Pat Porter requests was found (neither appears in the 2020–2021 grants summary).
figures: STARS $15,829 (2021); Animal Rescue request $20,000 (minutes 2021-03-16).
reasons: efficiency: requests are weighed together when the budget is built; 2021 budget already finalized (Mayor Earl Funk)
public: D.B. (STARS) and G.P./M.N. (Steinbach and Area Animal Rescue) presented requests.
notes: The 2022-09-20 mayor quote is already verified in the 2022–2026 report.

title: New Code of Conduct: unused Ethics Commission dropped, with reasons given in public; final version added from council mailboxes
summary: Responding to new provincial rules, council adopted Code of Conduct By-law 2158. Councillor Zwaagstra moved to delete the Ethics Commission section, explaining that the city had never created one and provincial rules now cover ethics. Second and third readings were added to the Oct 20 agenda at the meeting from material in council mailboxes.
status_detail: R20-187 (first reading as amended), R20-192 (agenda amended), R20-208/209 (second and third readings), all unanimous.
figures: Sanctions up to suspension without pay and a $1,000 fine (Zwaagstra, 2020-10-06, 0:15:33).
reasons: efficiency: Ethics Commission never created; out of date; disputes go to the province (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: None.
seconder: Damian Penner / Jake Hiebert / Bill Hiebert

title: New Traffic By-law: amendments, including fines and a public-request clause, directed at a September committee meeting
summary: Staff said the draft Traffic By-law 2164 went to a committee meeting in September 2020, where council directed changes (keeping residents' right to request traffic devices, removing a vehicle restriction, raising disabled-parking fines). The mover said there was nothing further to add; it passed unanimously.
status_detail: First reading R20-225 (Nov 3, 2020); second and third readings R21-018, R21-019 (Jan 19, 2021), unanimous.
figures: Disabled-parking fine $100 → $250 (Warkentin, 2020-11-03, 1:22:16).
reasons: staff-direction: council requested amendments at committee (Troy Warkentin, City Manager)
public: None.

title: Clearspring Greens plan rebuilt by Councillor Susan Penner after talking with residents; added to the agenda at the meeting
summary: With 78 objections registered, Councillor Susan Penner added a resolution to the Jan 5, 2021 agenda at the meeting to cancel the plan and replace it with a 50/50 split capped at $1,610 per lot, explaining that residents she spoke with would support it. It passed unanimously; the new plan drew 6 objections and was built in 2021.
status_detail: R21-011 and R21-012 (Jan 5, 2021); old By-law 2132 defeated R21-031 and new By-law 2168 R21-032/033 (Feb 16); third reading R21-076 and tender R21-077 (Apr 20, 2021). Debenture reduced to $136,850 (2022-02-15).
figures: Cap $1,610 per parcel; borrowing $233,450 authorized, $136,850 issued (Warkentin, 2021-02-16 0:09:21 and 2022-02-15 0:36:18); objections 78 → 6.
reasons: already-public-later: explained the revised plan and her consultations in public (Susan Penner)
public: Residents had filed 78 objections to the 2020 plan; 6 objected to the revised plan.
notes: The resolution was not on the published agenda; it was added at the meeting (R21-001).

title: Event centre land assembled through privately negotiated purchases, each ratified in public with the price
summary: The city bought downtown parcels for the event centre: 340 Hanover St. ($250,000, Jan 2021), 310 Hanover St. ($475,000, May 2021, on an offer signed by Southeast Event Centre Inc. and assigned to the city) and five Credit Union lots on Reimer Ave. ($1.4M, Apr 2022, on a same-day package). Each was negotiated privately, as land deals lawfully may be, and approved by public resolution with the price stated.
status_detail: R21-015, R21-097, R22-103 carried unanimously.
reasons: confidential-land: long-term downtown land strategy, described only "in general terms" until the project was known (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: None.
seconder: Jac Siemens / Damian Penner / Susan Penner

title: Administrative penalty by-law: "we discussed this at SPC and the consensus was" to proceed
summary: Amendments adding by-laws to the administrative penalty system were discussed at the April 13, 2021 SPC, which directed staff to bring first reading. The mover said the SPC consensus was to proceed; it passed unanimously.
status_detail: R21-092 (first reading) carried unanimously.
reasons: staff-direction: direction from council at SPC to proceed (Adam Thiessen, Corporate Services Manager)
public: None.

title: Affordable housing grant: process set at SPC; council departs from staff in public with reasons
summary: At the Sept 14, 2021 SPC, council agreed by consensus to extend the deadline for proposals for a $1.337M provincial affordable-housing grant. Staff recommended forwarding two of three proposals; at the public meeting Councillor Zwaagstra moved to forward only Steinbach Community Outreach's, explaining why, and council agreed unanimously.
status_detail: R21-232 carried unanimously.
figures: Provincial conditional grant $1.337M (Zwaagstra, 0:09:32).
reasons: staff-direction: deadline set by SPC consensus (Adam Thiessen, Corporate Services Manager)
public: Proposals from Steinbach Community Outreach, Habitat for Humanity (Southeast) and a private builder (organizations).

title: Procedures By-law 1809 (which closes study sessions) reviewed and kept without discussion of closed sessions
summary: At the Nov 2, 2021 organizational meeting council carried out the once-a-term review required by the Municipal Act (s. 149) of Procedures By-law 1809 and Organization By-law 2025. The only question was about quorum; both were accepted unchanged.
status_detail: R21-226: "Council reviewed and accepted Procedures By-Law 1809." Organization By-law 2025 accepted the same night.
reasons: municipal-act-allows: the Act requires a procedures by-law and a review once per term (Troy Warkentin, City Manager)
public: None.
notes: By-law 1809 dates from 2006; the version on the city website includes s. 12.1 closing study sessions. No amendment was found in 2018–2022 minutes, so the clause is assumed to have been in force in 2021, but the 2021 text was not seen.

title: By-law updates (business licences, burning, swimming pools) worked through at SPC before first reading
summary: Staff reported that new business licence and burning by-laws were discussed at the Nov 30, 2021 SPC and the swimming pool by-law at a September 2021 SPC "along with ... comments provided by council". Each passed every reading unanimously with short explanations.
reasons: no-decision-made: SPC used for systematic review of old by-laws before formal readings (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: None.
mover: Jake Hiebert; Jac Siemens; Michael Zwaagstra
seconder: Michael Zwaagstra; Damian Penner; Bill Hiebert

title: Honorary street naming policy: "much debate" at SPC, passed in under three minutes in public
summary: Staff said the honorary street naming policy had been debated at length at SPC and redrafted on council's advice. At the public meeting two councillors spoke briefly in favour and it passed unanimously.
status_detail: R22-094 carried unanimously (Case 1 in the existing 2022–2026 report).
reasons: staff-direction: comments and advice from SPC used to recraft the policy (Troy Warkentin, City Manager)
public: None.

title: Re-elected council holds a private orientation and a day-and-a-half fall budget study session (Nov 2022)
summary: Two weeks into the new term, Councillor Jake Hiebert told viewers that council had held a 3-hour orientation session and would spend a weekend day and a half at its fall study session 'to determine spending priorities for the city'. Neither session had a public notice, agenda or minutes; the priorities set there surfaced in the 2023 financial plan adopted in March 2023.
status_detail: The study session went ahead as announced. Its results became public only as part of the 2023 financial plan (R23-053, Mar 21, 2023, unanimous).
figures: Orientation 3 hours; fall study session a day and a half (transcript Nov 15, 2022, 0:00:16).
notes: The Nov 1, 2022 inaugural meeting (no transcript in the collection) ratified the mayor's appointments by resolution R22-244 (D. Penner / B. Hiebert, unanimous).

title: 2023 budget worked out in 'very long meetings' and weekends at study sessions
summary: Council adopted the 2023 financial plan unanimously after the required public hearing. In the vote the mayor described the work behind it as 'very long meetings' and weekends; Councillor Siemens later said the year's reserve transfers reflected decisions made 'in our study session' and other discussions.
status_detail: Adopted in public, unanimously (R23-053). The study-session deliberations themselves have no public record.

title: Traffic-signal complaints: provincial report-back first planned for SPC, then given at a public meeting (Jan–May 2023)
summary: Councillors Siemens and Zwaagstra raised complaints about PTH 12 signals. By consensus, council asked administration to meet Manitoba Transportation and Infrastructure (MTI). The mayor proposed hearing the result at an SPC meeting 'so we could go over this and just close the book on this'; the City Manager later recalled that MTI had presented to a council committee meeting in spring 2020. The update was in the end given at the public meeting of May 2, 2023.
status_detail: The City Manager reported MTI's completed signal review at the public meeting on May 2, 2023, not only at SPC.
reasons: efficiency: proposed taking the provincial department to SPC to go over the results (Earl Funk)
decision_source: minutes (Jan 3, 2023: 'Council consensus was provided to administration that administration meet with...')

title: Council expense policy reviewed at SPC, then adopted in public (Apr 2023)
summary: The mayor told the meeting the expense policy had been reviewed at SPC and that reviewing policies and by-laws is one of SPC's 'main goals'. Staff summarized what SPC had discussed (meal and entertainment limits) and the extra changes; Councillor D. Penner explained the changes in public before both expense policies passed unanimously.
status_detail: Adopted unanimously (R23-067 council, R23-068 employees), with the main change explained in public.
figures: City mileage rate 49 cents/km (transcript 0:10:47).
reasons: efficiency: reviewing policies and by-laws is one of SPC's main goals; the policy had already been worked through there (Earl Funk)

title: Asset management policy discussed at SPC; brought to a public vote because a federal grant required it (Oct 2023)
summary: Staff said the asset management policy and strategy had been discussed at the Sept 12, 2023 SPC meeting and that 'the reason it's here again today' was a condition of the FCM asset management grant that council approve it by resolution in a public meeting. It passed unanimously.
status_detail: Adopted by public resolution R23-199.
notes: 'FCA' is the transcript's rendering, most likely FCM (Federation of Canadian Municipalities).

title: Development fees: four options argued at SPC; council cuts the 7.5% discussed there to 5% in a public 5–2 vote (Sept–Nov 2023)
summary: Administration presented fee options at the Sept 12, 2023 SPC meeting and recommended a larger increase. At first reading Councillor Zwaagstra moved 5% a year instead of the 7.5% discussed at SPC, saying SPC was 'not a final decision'. Councillors Jake Hiebert and Damian Penner argued for 7.5% 'as discussed in our SPC'; D. Penner set out the four SPC options in public. By-law 2233 passed 5–2 at each reading.
status_detail: By-law 2233 adopted at 5% a year for four years (R23-211, R23-224, R23-225), each 5–2. The decision went against the figure favoured at SPC, and was made and explained in public.
figures: 5% a year for four years (R23-211); SPC options 2.5%, 5%, 7.5%, 10%, with a staff note that 11% would be needed to restore past contribution levels (D. Penner, Nov 7, 2023, 0:06:44–0:07:13); construction inflation 5–6% a year since 2012 (Zwaagstra, Oct 17, 2023, 0:17:50).
reasons: no-decision-made: the 7.5% at SPC was 'not a final decision'; council reflects and decides in public (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: No residents spoke. The SPC report was attached to the public package as background (City Manager, Oct 17, 2023), but the SPC debate itself was not public.
seconder: Jac Siemens (R23-211); Bill Hiebert (R23-224); Susan Penner (R23-225)
notes: Jake Hiebert quotes rest on medium-confidence speaker identification (reasoning in id_evidence).

title: 2024 budget 'based on the recommendations of council' at its November final review; no one speaks at the public hearing
summary: In September 2023 the mayor told council it would 'have to spend time this study session rethinking how we do things'. Presenting the 2024 financial plan, the Senior Manager of Finance said it was based on council's recommendations at its final review in November. No member of the public spoke at the hearing, and the plan passed unanimously.
status_detail: Adopted unanimously (R24-073).
figures: Municipal mill rate 14.4, an increase of just over 5%; capital program $62.7 million; revenues just under $38.5 million (transcript Apr 2, 2024, 0:05:52).
public: The mayor asked twice for comments at the financial-plan hearing; none were made (transcript 0:17:05).

title: Funding requests from community groups routinely sent to the closed budget study session (2023–2026)
summary: Rather than decide group funding requests in public, the mayor repeatedly proposed, and council agreed by consensus, to put them on the study-session agenda: minor hockey (Oct 2023), Eastman Raiders floodlights (May 2025), Southeast Events Group funding (June 2026), and Summer in the City 2027 funding (July 2026, 'deal with it in November'). The stated reason is that money requests should be weighed against the whole budget.
status_detail: This review found no separate public resolution answering the minor hockey or Raiders requests; any funding would appear only inside a later financial plan.
figures: Eastman Raiders sought about $70,000 of a floodlight project, covering about $141,000 themselves (delegation, May 6, 2025, 0:31:40).
reasons: efficiency: a 'financial ask' is best discussed 'at length with our budget in front of us'; fairer to the group and the city (Earl Funk); already-public-later: the July study session is 'where we build our budget', which is then finalized in November (Earl Funk)
public: Delegations (Eastman Raiders) presented in public; the decisions on their requests were moved to the study session.
decision_source: minutes (Oct 3, 2023: 'Consensus of Council was to consider it at its November study session for discussion'; May 6, 2025 consensus per transcript 0:39:27)
notes: Summer in the City request (Jul 21, 2026, 1:38:03–1:38:24) taken as information to be dealt with in November; quote not used because the short reply is on a merged speaker label.

title: Procedures By-law 1809, which closes every study session, reviewed and accepted unchanged (Nov 2023)
summary: At its organizational meeting council carried out the once-a-term reviews the Municipal Act requires: Organization By-law 2025 (which sets up the SPC as the whole council sitting as a committee), Procedures By-law 1809 and the Code of Conduct By-law 2158. All were 'reviewed and accepted'. By-law 1809 s. 12.1 closes every study session 'as all matters are in preliminary stages'.
status_detail: Accepted without recorded amendment or debate; the blanket closure of study sessions stayed in place. The 2026–2030 council had not yet reviewed By-law 1809 as of its Nov 3, 2026 inaugural meeting.
reasons: no-decision-made: study sessions are closed 'as all matters are in preliminary stages and will eventually be decided upon at a public meeting' (By-law 1809 s. 12.1 (council)); already-public-later: matters are to be decided later at a public meeting (By-law 1809 s. 12.1 (council))
resolution_no: R23-215 (Organization By-law 2025); R23-216 (Procedures By-law 1809); R23-217 (Code of Conduct By-law 2158)
notes: No transcript of the Nov 7, 2023 organizational meeting is in the collection, so whether there was any discussion is unknown. By-law text quoted from the existing report's reading of By-law 1809 s. 12.1.

title: Province, Canadian Centre for Safer Communities and Headway present a safety plan to SPC; council joins in public (Feb 2024)
summary: The presentation asking Steinbach to champion a community safety and well-being plan was given at the Jan 9, 2024 SPC meeting, not at a public council meeting. Staff summarized it in public on Feb 6 and council resolved to take part.
status_detail: Council voted to participate (R24-025, unanimous).
figures: Province funds the consultant and $60,000 per community for plan priorities (transcript 0:08:52).

title: Design and construction standards 'generally agreed to by council' at a committee meeting (Feb 2024)
summary: The City Manager said the city engineer had presented the changes to the standards for new development at a committee meeting in early January, that the detail was not included again in the public package, and that 'the updates that were discussed and generally agreed to by council' were now presented. Council approved them unanimously.
status_detail: Approved unanimously (R24-024). The supporting detail stayed out of the public record.
reasons: efficiency: details not repeated because council had already reviewed them and asked questions at committee (Troy Warkentin)

title: Sponsorship and naming-rights policy drafted from council's 'direction' at SPC (Feb–May 2024)
summary: The City Manager said the policy was developed after other cities' policies were reviewed at a February committee meeting, where 'requests and recommendations from council were forwarded to administration'. The minutes themselves record that the policy was 'prepared based on comments and direction of Council from the February 13, 2024 Strategic Priorities Committee meeting'.
status_detail: Adopted unanimously (R24-105).
reasons: staff-direction: policy drafted from council's requests and recommendations at the February committee meeting (Troy Warkentin)

title: One-bid, over-budget sewer force main tender decided on a package delivered the same day (Mar 2024)
summary: The Loewen Boulevard force main tender, which drew a single bid, was in a supplementary package left in councillors' mailboxes that day. Council awarded it unanimously.
status_detail: Awarded to Accurate HD Ltd. (R24-065, unanimous).
figures: Single bid of $570,310 plus taxes (transcript 2:19:08); award $491,693 plus taxes (minutes R24-065). The difference is not explained in the minutes text.

title: Supplier bankruptcy first raised at SPC, then reported in public (Nov 2024)
summary: A report at the previous week's SPC meeting mentioned that Shupack Equipment Inc., which held a 50% deposit on a garbage truck approved in 2020, had gone into receivership. The City Manager gave a follow-up report at the public meeting and answered questions.
status_detail: Reported in public for information; recovery through the receiver was still pending.
figures: Deposit of 50% of the original purchase price (transcript 0:12:01); amount not stated.
reasons: already-public-later: follow-up report on the SPC item given at the public meeting (Troy Warkentin)

title: Southeast Event Centre operating agreement added and approved on documents received that day (Jan 2025)
summary: The operating agreement handing the new event centre to Southeast Events Group Inc. was added to the agenda at the meeting and decided on an attachment put in councillors' mailboxes earlier that day.
status_detail: Agenda amended to add the item (R25-001); agreement approved (R25-003).

title: 2025 budget: grant decisions made at study session; Susan Penner asks for them to be visible in the grants line
summary: At the 2025 financial plan meeting Councillor Susan Penner said a cost 'we talked about this at study session' should appear in the grants line rather than 'getting lost' in the budget, asked for event centre operating support to be shown there, and asked for the Chamber of Commerce business-tax grant to be reviewed at the July study session; she repeated the Chamber request in April. The mayor agreed the Chamber grant should be 'relooked at at the next study session'.
status_detail: The 2025 financial plan passed unanimously (R25-048). No public result of the study-session review was found; the 0.5% Chamber business-tax levy was approved again on Apr 7, 2026.
figures: Chamber of Commerce receives the 0.5% business tax less a 5% administration fee (S. Penner, Apr 15, 2025, 0:31:14).

title: Zwaagstra recalls that downtown land talks with the credit union began in 'closed meetings' (history told Mar 2025)
summary: In an opening on the event centre's history, Councillor Zwaagstra said that early in his first term (from 2006) Mayor Goertzen told council 'in our initial closed meetings' to do everything possible to keep the Steinbach Credit Union downtown, leading to an agreement to build a new curling rink. Closed sessions on land negotiations are a lawful use of in-camera meetings.
status_detail: Historical account; the resulting agreement and curling rink were later public.
reasons: confidential-land: land and headquarters negotiations with the credit union began in closed meetings (Michael Zwaagstra)
notes: Events date from about 2006–2010, before this period; recorded because it was said in this period.

title: Economic development grant: councillors object to 'veils of transparency', request goes to study session, decision made in public (Mar–Aug 2025)
summary: During a delegation from Steinbach Economic Development about a federal immigration program, the director (M.B.) said she could not divulge how many places the city had been given. Councillor Susan Penner objected to being asked for taxpayer money without information, and Councillor Damian Penner called it 'veils of transparency'. The corporation's grant request was moved to the July study session at Councillor Siemens' suggestion. On Aug 5, 2025 council voted in public not to renew the five-year economic development office grant, with members explaining why.
status_detail: Grant not renewed after Dec 31, 2025 (R25-158, unanimous), decided and explained in public. That R25-158 answers the March request is likely but not confirmed in the minutes.
figures: City contribution $65,000 a year for five years, 2021–2025 (Siemens, Aug 5, 2025, 0:24:52).
reasons: already-public-later: request taken to study session, with a decision later made by public resolution (Earl Funk)
public: The delegate (M.B.) said program numbers were not public under the federal department's rules and offered to ask.
notes: Susan Penner's 1:16:10 quote is a medium-confidence identification (speaker map).

title: Five-year exclusive ice agreement decided on a same-day report; one-year-trial motion withdrawn (Sept 2025)
summary: The Eastman Selects' five-year agreement with the event centre came to council as a supplementary report delivered that day. Councillor Siemens moved to make it a one-year trial, then withdrew after staff explained council could only approve or reject it as a whole; he said he would 'begrudgingly' vote for it. Councillor Zwaagstra said he would not substitute his judgment for the City Manager's. A Manitoba GROW grant item that night was also 'information to follow'.
status_detail: Ratified unanimously (R25-179); the one-year amendment had no seconder and was withdrawn.
reasons: efficiency: SEG runs the centre with some independence; he deferred to the City Manager's review (Michael Zwaagstra)
notes: Parsed motions list Siemens' amendment as 'Lost (no seconder)'; the transcript shows he withdrew it (0:32:33).

title: Mayor discloses on the record that he met a developer (Oct 2025)
summary: At first reading of a 36-unit rezoning at 635–641 Main Street, Mayor Funk said he had met the developer and wanted to hear the neighbourhood's views at the hearing. The related parking variance, which staff recommended denying, was later approved 5–2 after a long public debate.
status_detail: Variance V-2025-32 approved 5–2 on Nov 18, 2025 (R25-222; against: Jake Hiebert, Michael Zwaagstra).
figures: 36 units (existing report).
notes: Unit count and staff recommendation taken from the existing report (verified there).

title: Road-widening by-law added to the agenda and passed on a same-day package (Nov 2025)
summary: Second and third readings of By-law 2269 (Friesen Avenue road widening, subject to an expropriation-by-consent agreement) were added to the agenda at the start of the meeting, from a supplementary package left in mailboxes that day.
status_detail: Agenda amended (R25-207); By-law 2269 given second and third readings (R25-216, R25-217), unanimous.

title: 2026 'flood' budget: projects chosen over two days at the November study session; 'direction of council' cited to residents
summary: After the September 2025 storm, residents' questions about drainage were sent to the November study session. Even a senior manager said he was 'not privy to' the study-session agenda. The 2026 financial plan, with a $35.8 million capital program, was adopted unanimously; the mayor and Councillor Siemens said the flood projects were set over two days at the November study session, and staff said further programs were 'presented at committee to council last week'. Asked by a resident about a sewer reroute, the mayor answered that 'It was the direction of council'.
status_detail: Financial plan adopted unanimously (R26-058). The study-session reasoning was summarized in public, but its options and trade-offs were not.
figures: $35.8 million capital program (Mayor, Mar 17, 2026, 0:29:41).
reasons: already-public-later: the study-session promise is delivered in the public budget (Earl Funk)
public: A resident (M.R.) spoke at the Oct 21, 2025 delegation and the Mar 17, 2026 hearing about repeated basement flooding and asked about the sewer reroute.

title: Regular meetings are recorded and livestreamed; councillors note the public meetings are short (2025–2026)
summary: Members repeatedly acknowledged that every word of regular meetings is recorded and streamed online. In his farewell opening Councillor Zwaagstra said there was no 'deep, dark secret' to reveal, urged people to watch the YouTube videos, and noted the public meetings 'typically last only about an hour'. The mayor asks speakers to give their name and address 'because everything's recorded'.
status_detail: Regular meetings continued to be recorded and posted throughout the period; SPC and study sessions are not recorded.

title: Five-year event centre lease added late and ratified on information given that afternoon (Jan 2026)
summary: A long-term lease between Southeast Events Group Inc. and a sporting-goods retailer, which needed council's ratification as building owner, was added as a late item; the City Manager said council received the information that afternoon.
status_detail: Agenda amended (R26-001); lease ratified subject to an MOU (minutes item 19, unanimous).
figures: Five-year lease plus five-year renewal (existing report).
resolution_no: minutes item 19 (resolution number not shown in extracted text)

title: Sump-pump and land-drainage by-law: first presented at committee, then explained and passed in public (Mar–Aug 2026)
summary: Staff told council in public that a review of Sump Pump By-law 1674 had been recommended 'at committee to council last week'. The new Land Drainage By-law 2274 got first reading on May 19, 2026 and second and third readings on Aug 4, when Councillor Zwaagstra explained its purpose in public, noting it had been discussed at SPC and at first reading.
status_detail: By-law 2274 adopted (R26-102 first reading; R26-162 and R26-163 second and third readings), unanimous.
reasons: already-public-later: discussed at SPC and at first reading; purpose explained again at final readings (Michael Zwaagstra)
mover: Jake Hiebert (R26-102); Michael Zwaagstra (R26-162); Damian Penner (R26-163)
seconder: Michael Zwaagstra (R26-102); Jake Hiebert (R26-162); Bill Hiebert (R26-163)
notes: That the Aug 4 remarks concern By-law 2274 is inferred from the minutes (Zwaagstra moved R26-162) and his description ('nuisance water and sump pumps').

title: Closed meetings held after council adjourns, with no closure resolution or subject in the minutes (Mar and Jul 2026)
summary: At the end of the Mar 17, 2026 meeting the mayor announced 'There's a closed meeting to follow council'. On Jul 7, 2026, after adjournment, he asked the City Manager whether a closed meeting was still necessary. Neither set of minutes records a resolution to close, the ground under s. 152(3) of the Municipal Act or the general nature of the matter.
status_detail: No resolution to close, ground or subject appears in the minutes of Mar 17 or Jul 7, 2026; what was discussed is unknown.
notes: No reason for closing was stated in public. The Code of Conduct By-law 2158 itself provides for an in-camera review of complaint reports followed by a public vote, which shows the city knows the close-then-decide-in-public pattern.

title: $200,000 provincial public safety grant: decision deferred to an August SPC meeting; no public resolution found (Apr–Oct 2026)
summary: A $200,000 provincial 'security rebate' was received as information on Apr 7, 2026. On Jul 21 staff proposed $65,000 for a second community safety officer truck and $135,000 for security cameras, saying such items would normally go to SPC first. Councillor Susan Penner preferred an SPC discussion, citing privacy; Councillors Siemens and Zwaagstra asked about library cameras. The City Manager noted it could simply come back to one of two regular August meetings, but by consensus council deferred it to Aug 11, which the mayor called a special meeting of council and Councillor Zwaagstra 'an SPC meeting'.
status_detail: No resolution on the grant appears in the minutes of Aug 4, Aug 18, Sept 1, Sept 15 or Oct 6, 2026, or on the Oct 20 agenda. Resolution numbers run without a gap from R26-166 (Aug 4) to R26-167 (Aug 18), so no numbered council resolution was passed on Aug 11.
figures: $200,000 (minutes Apr 7, 2026 item 32; transcript 1:47:46); staff options $65,000 CSO truck and $135,000 cameras (transcript Jul 21, 2026, 1:22:18).
reasons: staff-direction: administration would normally take such an allocation to SPC first (Adam Thiessen); candid-discussion: wanted an SPC discussion to understand the rationale, including privacy in public places (Susan Penner)
decision_source: minutes Jul 21, 2026 item 44: 'Consensus of council was to defer the decision until a Strategic Priority Committee meeting could be held on August 11, 2026.'
notes: Whether the Aug 11 meeting was held, and what it decided, could not be confirmed. The Oct 20, 2026 overnight security contract (Next Level Servicing, $148,000 for 2027) is a separate item funded from the 2027 budget.

title: Request made at a committee meeting is decided by public resolution after Zwaagstra asks 'resolution or consensus?' (May 2026)
summary: Steinbach Community Outreach and Eden Healthcare Services first asked for an endorsement 'at committee meeting'. When the written request reached council, Councillor Zwaagstra asked whether a resolution or a consensus was needed; the City Manager replied that resolutions are better, and council passed one.
status_detail: Endorsement of The Bridge on Third adopted by resolution R26-096, unanimous.

title: $400,000 loan to the event centre operator: case made 'in committee', terms stated in public (June 2026)
summary: By-law 2272 lending money to Southeast Events Group Inc. was described as 'discussed previously at committee', where the event centre had explained its finances. The amount was not stated at first reading; at second and third readings Councillor Zwaagstra set out a $400,000 loan repaid over four years.
status_detail: By-law 2272 passed all three readings unanimously (R26-115, R26-125, R26-126). The event centre's own financial explanation was given only to the committee.
figures: $400,000 loan, repaid over four years (Zwaagstra, Jun 16, 2026, 0:39:07).
reasons: already-public-later: terms explained in public at final readings (Michael Zwaagstra)
mover: Damian Penner (R26-115); Michael Zwaagstra (R26-125); Bill Hiebert (R26-126)

title: Mayor welcomes a request made 'publicly' so there is 'a trail of paper' (Jul 2026)
summary: Council agreed to issue tax receipts for donations to replace the Steinbach Golf Club's bridges. The mayor said he was glad the club had asked publicly, so that any budget line would have a paper trail.
status_detail: Approved by resolution R26-144, unanimous.

title: Mayor and deputy mayor reject a resident's suggestion of favouritism at the Bridgepark Manor hearing (Jul 2026)
summary: At the hearing on Bridgepark Manor's six-storey seniors building, a resident (M.R.) said Steinbach has 'a culture of helping out the guy you know and passing things', adding she was not commenting on this project (an unproven allegation). The mayor called it speculation and 'not what goes on'; Councillor Zwaagstra said public hearings matter. Council approved the variance with 1.25 parking stalls per unit, not the 1.0 sought, 6–1.
status_detail: Variance V-2026-14 approved 6–1 (R26-147; against: Jac Siemens).
figures: Six storeys; parking ratio 1.25 per unit (R26-147).
reasons: no-decision-made: rejected any suggestion that decisions are made before the hearing: 'it's not what goes on' (Earl Funk)
public: Resident M.R. alleged a culture of favouritism (unproven) and said she was not commenting on this project. SteinbachOnline (Jul 28, 2026) quoted the mayor: 'We do not make decisions before the public hearing', and Zwaagstra rejecting 'back room deals'.
notes: SteinbachOnline quotes are from the existing report (external source, not re-checked here).

title: Last meeting of the term sends two funding requests to the new council's study session; Nov 3 regular meeting cancelled for orientation (Oct 2026)
summary: At the final meeting of the 2022–2026 council, the mayor proposed sending the Southeast Events Group's request for $20,000 a year for three years to host the Grand Slam of Curling, and Agape House's request for a grant in lieu of taxes, to the study session 'because it's a budget item'. Council agreed. It also cancelled the Nov 3 regular meeting so new councillors could receive orientation before Nov 17.
status_detail: Both requests await the new council's budget study session; Oct 20 minutes were not yet available to confirm how the referrals were recorded.
figures: $20,000 a year for 3 years, said to unlock $150,000–$160,000 a year in outside funding (Mayor, 0:39:02).
reasons: efficiency: 'because it's a budget item' — weighed at the study session (Earl Funk)
public: Agape House (192 Friesen Avenue) wrote asking for a municipal grant; Southeast Events Group wrote about the host fee.
notes: The mayor says "Cafe House" in the transcript; the agenda lists the item as Agape House, Request for Municipal Grant - 192 Friesen Avenue.

title: New council's inaugural meeting: mayor's appointments ratified by resolution after a staff point of order; no procedure or committee set-up on the agenda (Nov 3, 2026)
summary: The 2026–2030 council took the oath, received Code of Conduct By-law 2158 (which commits councillors to 'conduct and convey council business in an open and public manner' and provides for in-camera review of complaint reports followed by a public vote) and the mayor announced his appointments: Susan Penner deputy mayor and Hanover joint committee; Ron Falk library board; Councillor (B.) Hiebert watershed district; Susan and Damian Penner community development corporation; Greg Carlos La Broquerie joint committee; Damian Penner RCMP advisory committee (with Adam Thiessen replacing the mayor); Jake Hiebert Eastman Regional Municipal Committee. The mayor was moving to adjourn when staff raised a point of order that council should ratify the appointments by resolution; council then did so. The agenda had no review of the procedures by-law and no SPC or study-session schedule.
status_detail: Appointments ratified by resolution (minutes not yet available; mover and seconder from transcript). Library citizen appointments deferred to Nov 17. The Act requires the new council to review its procedures and organization by-laws once during its term; the previous council did so at its Nov 2023 organizational meeting.
mover: Councillor Hiebert (transcript 'Councillor Hebert'; which Hiebert is unclear)
notes: 'JCAP Library' is the transcript's rendering of the Jake Epp Library. The Seine Rat Roseau Watershed District's minutes, published in council's Oct 20, 2026 package, record motions to go in and out of camera (e.g. 181-2026, 182-2026) — a practice Steinbach's own minutes do not follow.
